consensus_summary: The dragon’s settled primary identification is Satan/the Devil (the ancient serpent), the personal adversary who deceives, accuses, and persecutes God’s people, as explicitly stated in Revelation 12:9 and 20:2; OT chaos-monster and empire imagery supply background layers rather than rival cores.
book_summary: The dragon is the devouring spiritual power behind earthly beasts and kingdoms, identified as the Devil and Satan, who gives its power, throne, and authority to the beast.
consensus_core_identification: Satan/the Devil (explicitly the ancient serpent of Revelation)
book_core_identification: the devouring spiritual power behind earthly beasts/kingdoms, identified as the Devil and Satan
boundary_disagreement: none; both treat OT empire/chaos dragons (Pharaoh, Babylon, Leviathan) as background or agents of the same satanic power rather than competing primary referents
rationale: Both cores name the identical referent—Satan/the Devil—using the same explicit Revelation texts; the book’s added phrasing about empowering beasts simply restates the consensus description of the dragon’s activity in Rev 13 and does not narrow, broaden, or replace the central identification.
strongest_objection: The book’s emphasis on ‘behind earthly beasts and kingdoms’ plus the Pharaoh/Babylon citations might be read as prioritizing political agents over the personal Satan, but the entry itself explicitly equates the two.
